$comment: APRA CPS 234 → ISO/IEC 27001:2022 mappings. Derived from APRA CPG 234 (Jun 2019) which itself benchmarks against the ISO 27000 series, plus the AustCyber CPS 234 → ISO 27001 cross-walk and the cross-walks published by Vanta/Drata/AuditBoard. CPS 234 obligations are outcome-oriented and most map to multiple ISO controls; we encode the strongest relationships rather than an exhaustive catalogue. relationship: 'partial' = overlapping intent but ISO control is broader/narrower; 'informs' = ISO clause/control directly addresses the obligation but is not a one-for-one substitute.
source: APRA CPG 234 (Jun 2019) + AustCyber CPS 234 ↔ ISO 27001 cross-walk

mappings.rationale: Board accountability for information security mirrors the leadership and commitment clause of the ISMS.
Approval and direction by management for information security policies.
Information security roles and responsibilities are documented and assigned.
Segregation of duties between conflicting information security roles.
Resources required to establish, maintain and continually improve the ISMS — i.e. the security capability.
Competence of persons performing work that affects information security performance.
Continual improvement of the ISMS to address changing threats and vulnerabilities.
Threat intelligence informing the maintenance of the security capability.
Information security in supplier relationships covers third-party capability assessment.
Addressing information security within supplier agreements.
Managing information security in the ICT supply chain.
Monitoring, review and change management of supplier services maintains capability through procurement and operations.
Information security for use of cloud services aligns with maintaining capability when assets are outsourced.
Internal audit and independent reviews provide objective assessment of capability.
Independent review of information security.
Information security policy framework approved and maintained — direct equivalent.
Policies provide direction and define responsibilities of all parties.
Management responsibilities — directing personnel to apply information security in line with policies.
Stakeholder responsibilities are documented.
Terms and conditions of employment include information security responsibilities.
Inventory of information and other associated assets.
Classification of information by criticality and sensitivity is the direct ISO equivalent.
Labelling of information drives downstream control selection based on classification.
Acceptable use of information and assets — handling rules driven by classification.
Information security risk treatment — selection and implementation of controls to protect assets.
Information security risk treatment — control implementation in operations.
Risk assessment based on criticality, sensitivity and threats drives the selection of controls.
Secure development life cycle ensures controls are commensurate at each stage.
Management of technical vulnerabilities across the asset lifecycle.
Configuration management throughout the lifecycle.
Change management addresses vulnerabilities introduced during the asset lifecycle.
Monitoring activities are embedded in BAU operations.
Access control as an embedded operational discipline.
Protection of information systems during audit testing — embedding controls in operations.
Monitoring, review and change management of supplier services provides ongoing assurance over third-party-managed assets.
Information security for use of cloud services — assurance over CSP-managed information assets.
Information security incident management planning and preparation.
Assessment and decision on information security events.
Response to information security incidents.
Learning from information security incidents.
Monitoring, measurement, analysis and evaluation — testing the effectiveness of controls.
Security testing in development and acceptance.
Compliance with policies, rules and standards for information security — periodic review of controls.
Internal audit of the ISMS — direct equivalent of CPS 234 internal-audit obligation.
Independent review of information security.
Contact with authorities — APRA notification of material incidents is the regulator-contact obligation.
Incident response procedures should include external regulatory notification.
Notification content overlaps with incident-response documentation requirements.
Contact with authorities also covers material control-weakness notification.
Material control weaknesses surface through compliance reviews and trigger notification.
Documented information — creating, updating and controlling records to demonstrate compliance.
